Attachment.description: A file or link that comes with a note.

file.description: Name of a file saved next to the test.

link.description: A web address, such as a page or a GitHub issue.

BlockKind.description:
What a block does, with its parameters and outgoing edges.

`next` is the block that runs afterwards; a block without `next` ends the run (or, inside a loop body, the current pass). Paths are relative to the folder of the test file.

oneOf.description: Launches an application and brings it to the front.

app.description: Bundle id; without it, the application under test opens.

arguments.description: Command-line arguments for an app that isn't running yet; a running one keeps its own.

environment.description: Environment variables, name to value, for an app that isn't running yet.

resetState.description: Quit a copy that is already running and start a fresh one that does not restore its windows, so every run begins from the same screen.

windowPosition.description: Move the main window once the app is up.

windowSize.description: Resize the main window once the app is up, so screenshots have the same size.

oneOf.description: Opens files, web addresses or links into apps, each file from a fresh copy so the original stays intact.

app.description: Bundle id; without it, each file opens in its default application.

closeAfter.description: When the attempt ends, passed or not, quit the apps this block started and close the copies of the files it opened.

files.description: Relative file paths, `http(s)://` addresses, or links of a scheme an app registered, like `myapp://inbox` (these need format 3). It may instead be `res:` and the 16 lowercase hex digits of a label, which finds the file wherever it moves inside the project. A test that names a file by its label is saved in format 2.

modifiers.description: Keys held down during the click.

waitForChange.description: After clicking, wait until the screen changes; fail if it does not.

oneOf.description: Moves the pointer onto the target and leaves it there, to bring up tooltips and menus that open on hover.

modifiers.description: Keys held down while the pointer moves.

waitForChange.description: After moving, wait until the screen changes; fail if it does not.

oneOf.description: Presses the button on `from`, moves to `to` holding it down, and lets go there.

modifiers.description: Keys held down during the drag.

waitForChange.description: After letting go, wait until the screen changes; fail if it does not.

oneOf.description: Turns the scroll wheel with the pointer over `at`, or over the middle of the window.

modifiers.description: Keys held down while the wheel turns: `cmd` zooms in most applications.

waitForChange.description: After scrolling, wait until the screen changes; fail if it does not.

oneOf.description: Types text, optionally clicking into a field first.
Presses one key combination, e.g. `cmd+shift+s`.
Waits for the screen to reach a state; fails after `timeout`.

timeout.description: A time: a whole number and `ms`, `s` or `m`, such as `500ms`, `10s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description: Waits a fixed time, whatever the screen shows.

duration.description: A time: a whole number and `ms`, `s` or `m`, such as `500ms`, `10s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description: Fails the run unless the screen matches the reference, or an element of the window is as expected.
The screen matches the reference.
An element of the window is as expected.
Goes to `then` if the condition holds, else to the first of `elseIf` whose condition holds, otherwise to `else`.
The screen matches the reference.
A value, usually a run variable, compares with another.
An element of the window is as expected.
Runs the chain starting at `body` `times` times, then goes to `next`. The body loops by linking back to this block.
Runs the chain starting at `body` once per row of a CSV file, then goes to `next`. Row values are available as `${data.COLUMN}`.

file.description: Path of the CSV file, relative to the folder of the test. It may instead be `res:` and the 16 lowercase hex digits of a label, which finds the file wherever it moves inside the project. A test that names a file by its label is saved in format 2.

oneOf.description: Runs another test file in place, as a sub-process: a test, or a block of the project's own (a `*.block.json` file).

inputs.description: Values of the `${input.NAME}` placeholders in the test it runs, by name. They may hold placeholders themselves, filled in where this block runs.

package.description: The version and address of the package `test` belongs to, as its author had it installed: what a person needs to install it again when it is missing.

oneOf.description: Runs a script. Inputs reach it as environment variables; it writes its outputs as `name=value` lines to the file named by `$JEV_OUTPUT`, and they become `${var.NAME}`. A script that exits with a code other than 0 fails the block.

timeout.description: A time: a whole number and `ms`, `s` or `m`, such as `500ms`, `10s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description: Runs a command line with `zsh -c`; fails unless it exits with `exitCode`.

folder.description: Folder the command runs in, relative to the folder of the test; without it, there.

saveOutput.description: Run variable that gets what the command printed, without the last line break.

timeout.description: A time: a whole number and `ms`, `s` or `m`, such as `500ms`, `10s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description: Sends an HTTP request; fails unless the answer has the expected status.

save.description: Parts of the answer kept as run variables.

timeout.description: A time: a whole number and `ms`, `s` or `m`, such as `500ms`, `10s` or `2m`.

url.description: May contain placeholders, as may header values and the body.

oneOf.description: Waits until a file reaches a state; fails after `timeout`.

path.description: Relative to the folder of the test, absolute, or from the home folder (`~/`); may contain placeholders.

timeout.description: A time: a whole number and `ms`, `s` or `m`, such as `500ms`, `10s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description: Runs an SQL query on an SQLite database file. With `expect`, runs it again until the answer is as expected, and fails after `timeout`.

file.description: Relative to the folder of the test, absolute, or from the home folder (`~/`); may contain placeholders.

saveAs.description: Run variable that gets the first value of the first row.

timeout.description: A time: a whole number and `ms`, `s` or `m`, such as `500ms`, `10s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description: Puts text or a picture on the clipboard, reads its text, a picture or a list of files into a run variable, or checks the text it holds.
Replaces the clipboard with the text, which may contain placeholders. Whatever the clipboard held before is gone, and the text stays there after the run.
Replaces the clipboard with a picture: the path of a PNG, or `${var.NAME}` of a variable of type image.

image.description: Path of a PNG file, or `${var.NAME}` of a variable of type image. It may instead be `res:` and the 16 lowercase hex digits of a label, which finds the file wherever it moves inside the project. A test that names a file by its label is saved in format 2.

oneOf.description: Keeps what is on the clipboard as a run variable: its text, a picture (a variable of type image) or the list of files, as text with one path to a line.
Waits until the text on the clipboard passes the test against `to`, which may contain placeholders; fails after `timeout`.

timeout.description: A time: a whole number and `ms`, `s` or `m`, such as `500ms`, `10s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description: Keeps the current date and time, written as `format` and moved by `shift`, as the run variable `saveAs`.

language.description: Language of month and day names; without it, the language the app runs in.

timeZone.description: Time zone the time is told in, an IANA name such as `Europe/Berlin` or `UTC`; without it, the time zone of the computer the test runs on.

CanvasContent.description: The drawing of a test on the editor canvas: blocks placed by hand, section frames and sticky notes. Coordinates are canvas points from the top-left corner.

positions.description: Top-left corners of blocks, by block id. Empty: every block is laid out automatically.

CanvasSection.description: A titled frame that groups the blocks drawn inside it, like a heading in a text.

frame.description: Where it is drawn, in canvas points from the top-left corner.

DatabaseExpect.description: What a database query must answer.

oneOf.description: The first value of the first row, as text; may contain placeholders.
How many rows the query returns.

ElseIf.description: One more exit of an `if`: taken when the earlier conditions did not hold and this one does.

oneOf.description: The screen matches the reference.
A value, usually a run variable, compares with another.
An element of the window is as expected.

ExpectStatus.description: Status the answer must have: `success` for any of 200–299, `any`, or one status code.

oneOf.description: Changed since the run started, or created during it.
Exists and contains the text, which may contain placeholders.

Modifiers.description: Keys held down: a list of `cmd`, `shift`, `option` and `ctrl`.

NamedValue.description: A name with a text, such as a script input or an HTTP header.

Note.description: A sticky note on the canvas.

anchor.description: What the note is about; a block's note moves with the block.

attachments.description: Files and links that come with the note.

author.description: Who wrote the note; empty when unknown.

frame.description: Where it is drawn, in canvas points from the top-left corner.

replies.description: The discussion under the note, oldest first.

resolved.description: Set when the discussion is settled.

time.description: When the note was written, as an RFC 3339 timestamp; empty when unknown.

oneOf.description: The whole test; what notes without an anchor in older files are about.
One block of the test.
The folder the test is in, and so all tests in it.

PackageNeed.description: The version of a community block a test was written with, and where to get it.

source.description: An https address of a repository, release or zip file.

Point.description: A point in fractions (0–1) of the window, from the top-left corner.

Priority.description: How much it matters that the test passes.

Rect.description: A rectangle in fractions (0–1) of the image or window, from the top-left corner.

Reference.description: A reference image (how the screen should look) and how to compare the screen with it.

area.description: Part of the image to compare; without it, the whole image.

compare.description: `similar`: at least `threshold` alike; `exact`: pixel by pixel; `meaning`: a vision model judges that the screen shows what `expect` says, or means the same as the image when there is no `expect`.

expect.description: For `meaning`: what the screen must show, in words.

hide.description: Parts painted over in grey before a screenshot is sent anywhere or stored in a report.

ignore.description: Parts left out of the comparison: clocks, avatars, counters.

image.description: Path of the reference image, relative to the folder of the test. A check by meaning with `expect` may leave it out. It may instead be `res:` and the 16 lowercase hex digits of a label, which finds the file wherever it moves inside the project. A test that names a file by its label is saved in format 2.

model.description: For `meaning`: the model of that provider to ask instead of its chosen one.

provider.description: For `meaning`: the AI provider to ask instead of the one chosen in the settings.

threshold.description: How alike the screen must be for `similar`, above 0 and at most 1.

Reply.description: One message in the discussion under a note.

author.description: Who wrote it; empty when unknown.

id.description: Unique among the replies of the note.

time.description: When it was written, as an RFC 3339 timestamp; empty when unknown.

Resolved.description: Who settled the discussion under a note, and when.

time.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp; empty when unknown.

SavedValue.description: A part of an HTTP answer kept as the run variable `name`. `from` is `status`, `body`, a field of a JSON body such as `body.items[0].id`, or a header such as `header.Location`.

ScriptInput.description: A value a script reads from the environment variable `name`, as `type`.

value.description: May contain placeholders; for an image, the path of a PNG file. It may instead be `res:` and the 16 lowercase hex digits of a label, which finds the file wherever it moves inside the project. A test that names a file by its label is saved in format 2.

ScriptOutput.description: A value a script reports, kept as the run variable `name`.

ScrollDirection.description: Which way a scroll moves the view: `down` brings what is further down into sight.

ScrollUnit.description: What the amount of a scroll counts: wheel notches (lines), or points on screen.

Simulator.description: An iOS Simulator device that runs the application under test. Tests act on the device's screen as it shows in the Simulator window, and look at it as the device draws it.

device.description: The device as Xcode lists it, like `iPhone 17`, or its identifier (UDID). Of devices with the same name, one already started is used, else the one with the newest iOS.

install.description: The app build (a `.app` folder) installed on the device before the application starts: relative to the test file's folder or absolute, and may contain placeholders such as `${env.NAME}`. Without it, the application must be installed already.

Target.description: Where on screen an action happens.

oneOf.description: Found by look: the image of the element, located on the current screenshot. It may instead be `res:` and the 16 lowercase hex digits of a label, which finds the file wherever it moves inside the project. A test that names a file by its label is saved in format 2.
A fixed point, in fractions of the window size.
The middle of an area: `x,y,width,height` in fractions of the window size, or `${var.NAME}` of a variable of type area.
Found by AI: the element described in words, like "the blue Save button".
Found by accessibility: the middle of an element of the window.

TestStatus.description: Where the test is in its life: being written, ready to run, or out of date.

TestType.description: What kind of test it is.

TimeShift.description: How far the date and time of a `dateTime` block are moved: negative goes back.

ValueCheck.description: `of` `is` `to`: `${var.status}` equals `200`. Both sides may contain placeholders.

ValueKind.description: What a value a script takes or gives is.

oneOf.description: Kept as `true` or `false`.
The path of a PNG file: absolute, from the home folder (`~/`) or relative to the test.
A rectangle in fractions (0–1) of the window as `x,y,width,height`: `0.1,0.2,0.5,0.3`.
Both sides read as numbers.
The reference shows up on screen.
The reference is no longer on screen.
The screen stops changing.
An element of the window is as expected.

WindowPosition.description: Where the top-left corner of a window sits on the screen, in points. The origin is the top-left corner of the main display; a display to its left or above has negative numbers.

WindowSize.description: The size of a window in points.

description: A JEVision test: a flowchart of blocks that drive and check an application. Tests are `*.flow.json` files; `*.block.json` files are blocks of the project's own, `*.template.json` files are templates, and `flow.json` is the test inside a community block.

$schema.description: Address of this schema, so that editors check the file and suggest its keys.

app.description: Bundle identifier of the application under test, e.g. `com.apple.TextEdit`.

author.description: Who wrote the test or looks after it.

blocks.description: Blocks by id, in any order; saved in the order the flow reads.

canvas.description: How the test is drawn; changes nothing in how it runs.

dependsOn.description: Tests that must pass before this one runs, as paths relative to the folder of this test file. When one of them fails, this test is blocked instead of run.

flaky.description: Someone marked the test as flaky: it sometimes fails for reasons outside the app.

format.description: Version of the layout of the file. JEVision doesn't open a file in a format newer than it knows.

icon.description: SF Symbol shown for a block made of this test (a `*.block.json` file); without it, the default one.

link.description: Web address of the issue or requirement the test covers.

minVersion.description: The oldest JEVision that can open the file, such as 1.4.0. An older one asks to be updated instead of opening it.

name.description: Name of the test, as lists and reports show it.

platform.description: Where the test is meant to run, such as `macOS 26`.

preconditions.description: What must be true before the test starts, such as `Signed in as a teacher`.

retries.description: How many times a failed run is retried before it counts as failed; without it, as many as the project says.

simulator.description: The iOS Simulator device the application runs in; without it, the application runs on this Mac.

start.description: Id of the first block to run.

tags.description: Words to sort and find tests by.
